title: Daughters mourn father killed by Mounties
article: The daughters of a man shot dead by Mounties are asking for privacy as they mourn the loss of their father.
Darby Mahon was fatally shot inside his Onoway apartment building by two RCMP officers Wednesday evening.
Mounties say he armed himself with a machete and was confronting a man in the same building who had allegedly assaulted his daughter.
One of Darby's daughters said the family would not be commenting, and need time to come to terms with what has happened.
Mounties were called to the apartment building on Lac Ste. Anne Trail around 7:30 p.m. after receiving a disturbance call.
A resident who lives above Mahon recalled the incident and said, Mahon busted opened the door of the basement level-suite to confront the man who he believed had assaulted his daughter.

"They (responding officers) heard him saying, 'I'm going to kill you. I'm not leaving this place until you're dead.' All he wanted was for the man to confront him," said the resident who heard four shots fired.
The Alberta Serous Incident Response Team (ASIRT) says when two members arrived at the apartment, they were confronted by a man with an edged weapon.
ASIRT executive director, Clifton Purvis, said "several" shots were fired and investigators are now waiting for the autopsy to be completed.
